state.case_summary:
A 30-year-old Asian man presented with a 6-month history of recurrent pain localized to the lateral side of his left knee. On examination, there was slight tenderness and swelling over the lateral joint line without other abnormalities. Plain radiographs were unremarkable, and routine laboratory tests were within normal limits. MRI demonstrated a 1.5 cm intra-articular space-occupying lesion invading the tibial plateau. On T1-weighted images, the lesion was homogeneous and isointense to muscle; on T2-weighted images, it appeared heterogeneous with internal specks and was unremarkable on fat-saturated T2 sequences. Gadolinium-enhanced MRI showed enhancement confined to the peripheral rim of the mass, with no satellite lesions identified.
